decision: Does the register keep one status column, or split into evidence basis, inference, disagreement and review?
constitution_ref: CLAUDE.md evidence status vocabulary; prompt-pack MELAKEELAWHOMADETHEPAST.md §10
options: keep the single status column | split into four separately recorded axes | keep one status and carry the other three in added columns
blocks: 03-REGISTERS/ schema and every register built on it; the shape of the inheritance rule
why_owner: A register schema decision, the same class as D-019
notes: Raised by the prompt-pack intake as PP-10. WHOMADETHEPAST §10 argues directly against a single flat scale: a claim can be well documented and contested, and a document can exist while its interpretation is uncertain, so evidence basis, assessment of the inference, disagreement and review status should be recorded separately. The objection has force and is not PP-3's question of competing vocabularies for one axis - the repository's seven values do conflate at least three things, and none can express "well documented and contested", which will be the ordinary condition of most rows. Against it: the single column is what makes the inheritance rule enforceable, since one field decides whether a claim may be built on, and a four-column scheme invites quiet promotion without a retrieval event. The single column stands until this is answered; the four axes can ride in notes meanwhile. The §14 claim lifecycle (draft/checked/reviewed/published/revised/withdrawn) rides on the same decision as a candidate review column.
